contract.blocking: The leaf is roughly 0.9 m wide by 2.0 m tall, standard door proportions: roughly twice as tall as wide. The round brass knob sits at adult hip height, about 1.0 m off the floor, on the LEFT edge of the leaf as viewed. A human standing at the door reads about 1.7 m tall against it: head below the top rail, knob at the hip. The door is never monumental and never miniature; it is an ordinary door a person walks through without ducking or reaching.

render.always: THE PLAIN DOOR: a single plain solid-wood door, warm honey-brown, with FOUR recessed panels (two small panels above two tall panels) and a round brass knob at mid-height on the LEFT edge as viewed. Slightly worn, ordinary, well-made. Standard proportions: the leaf roughly twice as tall as wide (about 0.9 m by 2.0 m). The door face NEVER carries lettering, a sign, or a plaque of any kind. The identical door design appears in every state and every era; only its surroundings change. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal.

master.bake: Face-on, door SHUT, set in an ordinary cream plaster wall with a simple wooden casing. The identity of record: four recessed panels (two small above two tall), round brass knob at mid-height on the LEFT edge as viewed, warm honey-brown wood, slightly worn and ordinary.

ajar.bake: The same door open a little toward the viewer, warm golden light spilling through the gap. By DEFAULT nothing is visible behind the door: no room, no landscape, no object, only warm light. A soft, warm, low-detail sliver of the room behind may appear ONLY when this spread's scene names it explicitly. Never darkness, never anything ominous through the gap.

museum.bake: The same door hung flat on a warm museum wall: honey wood floor, cream plaster, a soft spotlight from above, a small EMPTY brass plaque on the wall below/beside the door, and a velvet rope on brass stanchions in front. Frame, plaque, and rope never touch the door's face. NO lettering anywhere; the locked plaque is EMPTY.

prose.lore: The identical plain unlabeled door through which every era's founders walked. The book's argument is that it looked like nothing at the time and got its plaque only in hindsight: the same door in a dorm hallway, a city street, and a museum hall, and the repetition IS the thesis.
prose.rules: Pass the correct state sheet as reference on every render (master for shut, ajar for open, museum for the hall treatment), chained off the master identity. Per-spread scenes may relocate the door into any era's wall — a dorm hallway, a city street, a museum — but the leaf design never changes: same four panels, same honey-brown wood, same brass knob on the LEFT edge as viewed. Museum plaques carry per-spread exact quoted strings baked at render time; the locked museum sheet keeps its plaque EMPTY so no string leaks across spreads. The door face itself never carries lettering in any era or state. EARNED CHANGE 2026-08-09: the open-gap law was narrowed from 'never what is behind' to 'a soft warm scene-named sliver is legal' after takeoff-thursdays spread-19 (a warm desk/mug/whiteboard sliver through the ajar gap) was seen and accepted by the operator; warm-light-only remains the default, and darkness or ominous content through any gap remains banned outright.
